text.en: Shanti's parents plan a trip across India starting from the southern tip, Indira Point, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Shanti learns that Indira Point in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is the southernmost tip of India. An island is land surrounded by water on all sides, and India has over a thousand islands.
Their guide Rani takes them through the forest. Some trees are found only on these islands, with big roots spreading out at the bottom to support them.
Activity: roll a paper tube and see if it stands. Add small triangles at the base and it stays upright, like roots supporting a tree.
The forests are home to unique birds like the Andaman wood pigeon and the Andaman hornbill, found only here.
At the Marine Interpretation Centre they learn how tiny corals give shelter to many sea creatures. Life under the sea is as important as life in forests.
North Sentinel Island is home to people who live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors, so no one is allowed there. In 2004, when a tsunami struck, they survived, possibly by noticing signs in nature.
In the Sundarbans, mangrove roots help trees breathe in muddy salt water, hold the soil and stop waves from washing the land away. People nearby depend on the forest for daily needs.
People in the Sundarbans wear masks on the back of the head to confuse tigers, which attack from behind, as Appa heard.
Coir craft from coconut husk in Kerala is a zero-waste craft.

prompt.en: Why are corals and mangroves important?

requiredIdeas.en: Mangrove roots hold soil and stop waves

points.en: Indira Point is India's southernmost tip.
Island forests have unique plants and birds.
Corals and mangroves protect life and people.
